title: Magonia people arrested at Lyon, Agobard denies it

tellings.quote: where the whole Monagonia thing that Valet talks about. This is that period where you know you had these people supposedly coming from Mononia and some of them were arrested and then this bishop Agabard who was like a protorationalist came up with a justification for why this couldn't possibly be real.

plain: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, recalls a story that the researcher Jacques Vallee writes about, set around the 800s in Lyon, France. He says people were said to have arrived from a mysterious place called Magonia, some of them were arrested, and a bishop named Agobard, an early rational thinker, argued that it could not possibly be real. Jorjani tells it as an old example of a strange visitation being explained away by authorities.
